Triage first-touch (bare-card sweep): queued `pm:queue`, Task, `domain:services` (lands in `plugin-security`'s bootstrap loops + the position binder). Measured to R²=1.000 with the fix direction stated and uncontroversial: one `$in` existence read before each loop, and skip the UPDATE when the stored row equals the write — O(1) steady-state rebuild. Acceptance: the card's own rig readings re-run (slope 4.0 → ~0 on rebuild), or an equivalent counting-driver test in-repo if the cloud rig is out of reach (state which in the PR). Family note for the seat: #10945 (p0, engine — the quadratic registry scan) and #10979 (cli — inline seed) are the same boot-cost campaign from cloud#1555 — different packages/lanes, coordinate in PR bodies, no cross-lane fold.

## The card's measurement is unusually strong — inherit it, don't redo it

Slope **exactly 4.0000**, **R² = 1.000000** on both axes, with the per-statement histogram diff naming all four legs. And it carries its own **negative control**: on the same rig, objects/views/artifact seeds add **0.00** round trips each (0 → 400 objects all boot in 242), because schema sync is already batched through `TursoDriver.supports.batchSchemaSync`. **Identity content is the one content axis that is not.**

That control is what makes this a real finding rather than "loops are slow" — do not discard it, and say in your report whether it still holds.

## ⚠️ You cannot run the card's reproduction. Plan around it, don't fake it.

The reproducing commands live in **`objectstack-ai/cloud`**:

```
node scripts/dev-local/bootstrap-curve.mjs --hosted --permission-sets 0,5,10,20,40
```

**This session's GitHub access does not include `cloud`.** So you cannot re-run the curve, and you must not report a number as if you had.

What you *can* do, and what I want:
- measure **round trips** against a local driver double that counts calls — the card's own defect is a **count**, not a latency, and a count is measurable without the hosted rig;
- state the narrowing explicitly: the *latency* claim (171.7 ms per ms of RTT) is **inherited, not reproduced**.

⛔ Do not report an inherited number in a way that reads as measured. This lane has been wrong that way and it is the failure the whole report format exists against.

## The direction — both halves, and the second one is where the risk is

1. **Batch the read**: replace the per-item existence `SELECT` with one `find({ name: { $in: [...] } })` before the loop. The set is known in full before the loop starts.
2. **Skip the write when nothing changed**: an idempotent reconcile that writes unconditionally pays two round trips per item forever to change nothing.

⚠️ **Half 2 changes when writes happen.** Before you ship it, establish what — if anything — observably depends on the unconditional `UPDATE`. `updated_at` bumping on every boot is the obvious candidate; an audit trail or a change-feed consumer is the dangerous one. **If something does depend on it, stop and report** — that turns a performance fix into a behaviour change and it is not yours to make silently.

## What must be pinned — both directions

- **steady-state rebuild is O(1) round trips** for both loops: with N sets and N positions already seeded and unchanged, the count does **not** grow with N. Assert the count, not the wall time.
- ⚠️ **load-bearing — drift still reconciles**: a row whose stored value differs from what would be written **still gets its UPDATE**. An implementation that skipped all writes would show a beautiful curve and **stop reconciling entirely** — passing a round-trip-only suite while silently breaking the thing the loop exists to do. This is the leg that makes a vacuous pass impossible.
- **a genuinely new set/position is still created** — the batched read must not turn "absent" into "present".
- ⛔ **`null` is not "not mine"** (#3807): a batched `find` that cannot answer must not be read as "none of them exist", which would make every boot re-create everything. That is the same conflation class #10965 just fixed one package over — **judge the seam by whether it returned a result set.**

## Standing proof standard

Ablation with the signature predicted **first**; restore proved byte-identical by `git hash-object`, **and re-run the restore leg to a real verdict**. Prove `src/` vs `dist/` resolution argued from the files — prefer the falsifiable form (a `src`-only mutation flipping the verdict while `dist` bytes stay identical, marker absent from `dist`); two seats produced that today. Zero-hit counter-check with the **positive control run FIRST**. Gate union derived on the **final** commit, clean tree, `dispatch-gates.mjs` with **no path arguments**, exit codes captured before any pipe. Changeset required.

⚠️ **Class #10309 today**: the derivation was short on five services PRs and complete on four — the complete ones all **re-derived on the final committed diff**. Do that. One gate it can **never** name by construction: `check:optional-error-sink`.

⚠️ A gate's refusal (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET` / `--re-measure cannot run` / `Nothing was checked`) is **NOT MEASURED**, never a pass — build the closure and re-run. ⛔ **If a ratchet reddens, fix the code, never the baseline** — a seat did exactly that on `check:slot-lookup` today. ⛔ And if a **census** gate reddens naming a new import of yours, read its message: `check:driver-memory-census` reddened another PR of mine an hour ago and its own text says *"a new arrival is not a bookkeeping chore, it is the defect itself"*. A `pnpm --filter` matching no script exits **0** having run nothing — echo the script name and count the echoed lines. Never `git stash` (shared stack). Never report a grep hit count as a fact count.

⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/**` or `packages/spec` — zero ownership in this lane. ⛔ Do not reach into `cloud` — it is outside this session's access.

## Refs

`objectstack-ai/cloud#1555` (the 20 s request budget this competes for) · `bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts:166` · `TursoDriver.supports.batchSchemaSync` (the already-batched contrast) · #3807

PM review of PR #11116. **Accepted.** Reviewed against the branch by content.

## ⭐ The write-skip caveat found a load-bearing consumer — this is the finding

"Skip the write when nothing changed" is the kind of optimisation that quietly breaks whoever was counting the writes. It did, and the seat found it rather than shipping past it.

`security-plugin.ts:2840`'s publish materializer computed `applied = r.seeded + r.updated` and used that number **twice**: for the publish success/failure report, and for whether `reconcileAudienceBindingSuggestions` runs. Once the seeder stops re-writing converged rows, a **re-publish of an identical body** would have reported `success: false` and skipped the audience reconcile.

Verified in the diff; the comment states the reasoning exactly right:

> The question this line asks is "did the record end up matching the published body", **NOT** "was a write issued" — and until the seeder stopped re-writing rows it had nothing to change, those two were **accidentally** the same number.

And the safety argument is the part that makes it reviewable rather than plausible: all three refusal branches (foreign package, env-authored name, no owning package) leave `unchanged` at 0, **so every case that reported 0 before still reports 0**. That is a proof about the boundary, not an assurance.

Correctly classified as **not** a `needs_decision`: nothing observably *depends* on the unconditional write; one consumer depended on its *count*, and that consumer was fixed.

## ⭐ Writing the #3807 test broke the seat's own first implementation

> the lookup degraded to per-item reads which, against a double with no unique index, re-created all four rows

The fix is the one the principle actually demands: the lookup now reports **three** outcomes — present / absent / **unknown** — and **declines rather than inserts** on a read that could not answer. `null` is not "not mine" (#3807), and a seeder that treats an unanswerable read as "absent" duplicates rows on every boot.

Worth stating plainly: this is **stricter than the code it replaces**. The card asked for fewer round trips; the seat also closed a latent correctness hole it only found because it wrote the negative-direction test first.

## Two measurements at different layers, reconciled instead of contested

The card's figure is **4.0000 round trips/item, R² = 1.000000**, measured at `@libsql/client`. The seat's counter measured **2.0 facade calls/item → 0**, at the ObjectQL facade (one `find` + one `update` per item). Rather than presenting that as a correction, the report names the layer and shows the two agree at a **2:1 expansion**.

Both columns come from running the same counter twice — once with the four touched files reverted to `origin/main`, once at head. Steady-state rebuild: `n=1: 2→1 · n=5: 10→1 · n=20: 40→1 · n=40: 80→1`.

**Inherited, not reproduced — declared:** the `171.7 ms per ms of RTT (R²=0.998)` latency figure and the driver-level `4.0000` fit both come from `bootstrap-curve.mjs` in the cloud repo, which is outside this session's scope. The negative control (schema sync still adds 0.00) is **also inherited, by reading rather than re-measurement** — the 0→400-objects leg was not re-run, and the report says so instead of letting "still 0.00" read as freshly measured.

## Ablation: under-called, and the asymmetry is the interesting half

Predictions were written first. Leg A (restore the unconditional UPDATE): all five correct in **direction**, but breadth **under-called** — 4 red, not 2. Reported as a miss rather than retro-fitted.

The asymmetry is what I want on the record: **under leg A the pre-existing suite stayed 100% green.** The suite that existed before this card could not see this defect at all. That is the strongest available statement of why the new pins are load-bearing rather than decorative.

## Three ratchets reddened; all three repaired in code, no shrink-only baseline touched

- `check:engine-double-contract` — routed the double through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`; `--write` added one row to the **PINNED/tightening** ledger only, with `baseline.json` **verified untouched**. Confirmed in the diff: the only ratchet file in the surface is `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (+5).
- `check:where-matcher` — made the double **REFUSE** combinators rather than pretend to answer them.
- `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` — `TEST_DEBT 11→12` was the seat's **own** fixture (`TS2353`); it typed the fixture and returned to exactly 11, **entry not raised**. Run against a fully built closure (70/70), so a measurement rather than a refusal.

## ⚠️ Class #10309, caught in the act

Re-deriving the gate union **after the second commit** ADDED `check:entry-guard` and `check:parse-guard`. So the union is not a property of the card — it is a property of the *diff at a moment*, and deriving it once and reusing it silently drops families. This is the cleanest demonstration of that class I have seen today, and it argues for the rule the lane already follows: derive on the **final** commit, every time.

22 families green, each quoted by its own printed verdict line.

## Declared narrowings and scope

- The two dogfood real-engine seeding tests were **not** run locally — killed mid-boot twice by the 10-minute foreground ceiling behind a contended verify lock. A stand-in is named (the membership query shape is already shipping on both tables at `explain-engine.ts:389` and `security-plugin.ts:997`), and the gap is stated rather than papered over. CI runs them.
- **Scope note reported, not hidden:** the file face is one file wider than the claim named — `security-plugin.ts` took a one-line + comment change. That is the direct consumer of the contract this PR changed, required for correctness, not a drive-by. Reporting it is the right call; a wider face discovered by a reviewer reads very differently from one the author declares.

## Findings filed rather than ridden

- **#11096** — `bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities` seeds `sys_capability` with the identical per-item read + unconditional UPDATE. Same defect class, **third** table, and its count is the union of every package's `systemPermissions`, so typically larger than either axis this card measured. Searched for duplicates first.
- **#11097** — `reconcilePermissionSetProjection` projects env overlays one at a time and re-writes unconditionally. ⭐ Deliberately **not** folded in, with the reason measured: the env door stamps `customized`, which is outside what `recordDiffersFromBody` compares, so a naive skip would stop maintaining a flag the Setup list badges on. Its slope is unmeasured and the card says so.

That second one is the right kind of refusal — not "out of scope" as a shrug, but a specific mechanism explaining why the obvious transplant would break something.

## Open question — escalating

Whether the seeders should additionally declare `skipAutomations`. They write with `{isSystem: true}` but do not set it, so a metadata-bound automation on `sys_position` / `sys_permission_set` update fires today once per item per boot with an empty diff; after this PR it fires only on real drift.

The seat recommends **A for this PR, then C** (file it with a survey of whether any hosted environment actually binds an automation to these two system objects), and declined B because it changes which events tenant automations see on a **genuine drift repair** — a behaviour change beyond this card's remit. Nothing in the tree declares such an automation, so A is safe today. Agreed, and escalating C.

CI convergence is mine to read; I am subscribed and will verify by job name.
